title: Read a dashboard: rows, tabs, and links (preview)

blocks.content: Explore a dashboard on Grafana Play to see how rows and tabs group panels, and where a dashboard's introduction and links appear.
Explore the rows on Demo Wind Farm to see which panels each row groups together and how a row's heading stays visible when its contents are hidden.
Open the **Demo Wind Farm** dashboard.
Focus on the **Wind Farm Power** row heading.
This row groups a time series panel and a stat panel. A row can hold different types of panels. Its heading tells you what the panels cover before you read them.
Select the **Wind Farm Power** arrow to collapse the row.
The row's panels are hidden. The heading stays visible so you can expand the row again. Collapsing and expanding rows lets any viewer control what they see.
Select the **Wind Farm Power** arrow again to expand the row.
Find the row heading that starts with **Asset:**.
Take note that there are five panels using different formats.
Notice the **Alerts** row heading.
This row holds one panel, an alert list. The three rows form a logical progression: from the wind farm as a whole, to a single asset, to alerts.
Explore the top of Demo Wind Farm to see the text that introduces the dashboard and the links that point viewers to other pages.

blocks.title: Introduction and links on Demo Wind Farm

blocks.content: Open the **Demo Wind Farm** dashboard.
Focus on the **Introduction** panel.

This text panel opens the dashboard with its purpose. It also names the data source and gives instructions for exploring a panel. A viewer gets this context without having to work it out from the panels, which helps make the dashboard easy to interpret.
View the first link in the dashboard.

Dashboard links are displayed at the top of the dashboard. You can add links like this to a dashboard. Links let you navigate between commonly used dashboards or connect viewers to your visualizations, with shortcuts to other dashboards, panels, and external websites.
Explore the tabs on Time series graphs to see how a tab groups rows and shows one group at a time.
Open the **Time series graphs** dashboard.
Notice the **Time Series Introduction** tab is selected.
This tab groups the rows **Interpolation modes**, **Soft min & max**, **Multiple Y-Axes**, and **Dashed lines and bar examples**.
Select the **More Examples** tab.
Tabs let one dashboard hold what would otherwise be several smaller dashboards.
